title: When to Fine-Tune and How Big a Run You Need
summary: Fine-tuning changes the weights instead of the prompt. This lesson sets out when that pays for itself, then sizes a first run: trainable parameters and GPU memory for full fine-tuning, LoRA and QLoRA. The lessons after it walk through real fine-tuning runs end to end.
objectives: Decide between prompting and fine-tuning with a break-even calculation on token cost
Compute the memory of full fine-tuning from bytes per parameter
Count LoRA trainable parameters for a real model and target set
Choose between full fine-tuning, LoRA and QLoRA for a given GPU
prerequisites: Instruction tuning and loss masking from [Instruction Tuning](/learn/fine-tuning/instruction-tuning), the LoRA update from [LoRA and QLoRA](/learn/fine-tuning/peft-lora), and memory per parameter from [Training at Scale](/learn/training-and-adaptation/training-at-scale).
